key_insight: Influenza A and B in this subtropical Chinese city showed different weather triggers, and a hybrid DLNM-LSTM model could both explain these patterns and improve short-term forecasting.
clinical_relevance: Weather-informed surveillance may help public health teams anticipate subtype-specific influenza activity and better time prevention and resource planning.
method: 6 years of multi-site influenza surveillance data (2018-2023) from Putian were analyzed using influenza positivity rates.
Distributed lag non-linear models (DLNMs) estimated delayed, subtype-specific links between meteorological variables and influenza positivity.
A Bayesian-optimized LSTM combined meteorological, autoregressive, and socio-behavioral features for short-horizon forecasting.
evidence_signal: The model outperformed covariate-matched autoregressive baselines for both subtypes, with lower MAE and SMAPE, and was preliminarily evaluated in external data from Sanming.
watch_item: Forecast performance may depend on local surveillance quality and testing patterns, so portability beyond similar settings should be confirmed before operational use.
paper_title: Meteorological Drivers of Influenza A and B Positivity in a Subtropical Chinese City: A Six-Year Surveillance Study Integrating Distributed Lag Non-Linear Models and Deep Learning
